title: Konsulentbistand ved oppstart av Enova SFs nye svartjeneste
description: Enovas viktigste virkemiddel er investeringsstøtte til prosjekter, enten det er til store prosjekter i industrien eller til mindre tiltak i husholdningene. Enova skal forvalte felleskapets midler slik at disse gir størst mulig nytte for samfunnet. Gjennom å dekke en del av merkostnadene som markedet pådrar seg ved å velge mer energi- og klimavennlige løsninger, skal Enova bidra til å løfte frem klimaprosjekter. Enova driver også med veiledning. Enovas svartjeneste har vært driftet eksternt i over 20 år. Enova er nå i prosess med å håndtere denne tjenesten med egne ansatte. I mindre prosjekter gis det informasjon og råd, fortrinnsvis om Enovas støttetilbud, på Enovas nettsider, gjennom nyhetsbrev og Enovas veiledningstjeneste. Enova ønsker å inngå avtale om kjøp av konsulentbistand i forbindelse med etablering og drift av Enova SFs nye svartjeneste. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å sikre at Enova har tilstrekkelig kompetanse og kapasitet til å håndtere henvendelser og opplæring i en overgangsperiode frem til intern svartjeneste er fullt operativ. Oppdraget inkluderer konsulentbistand til veiledning rundt Enovas støttetilbud og Energimerkeordningen samt noe veiledning på temaer innenfor Enovas arbeidsområder. Ved utførelsen av oppdraget skal leverandøren betjene avtalte inn- og utgående henvendelser for Enova i tråd med svartjenestens fastsatte krav til kundestatistikk, inkludert svartid og kundetilfredshet. Konsulentene vil inngå i Enovas nyetablerte veiledningstjeneste, og arbeidsmetodikk og krav til tjenesten satt av Enova vil følges av konsulentene. Konsulentenes kontorsted kan være et annet enn Trondheim, men enkelte reiser til Trondheim i avtaleperioden må påregnes. Det estimeres et omfang for avtalen tilsvarende inntil 2 FTE (fulltidsekvivalenter) i perioden fra 01.03.27 til 31.12.27. Se konkurransegrunnlaget for en nærmere beskrivelse av oppdraget.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE GEM ACCELERATOR
description: Lahden seutu – Lahti Region Oy, operating under the name Business Lahti, requests tenders for the planning, implementation and operation of the GEM Accelerator. The GEM Accelerator is an international business accelerator focusing on the electrification, automation and digitalisation of mobility, transport and logistics. It is established through the Lahti GEM Supercluster project, funded by the European Regional Development Fund through the Helsinki-Uusimaa Regional Council. The Service includes detailed programme planning, national and international participant scouting, marketing and communications, management of the application and selection processes, implementation of three (3) accelerator batches, participant-specific support, partner and investor engagement, monitoring, reporting and final handover. At least eighteen (18) companies or teams shall be selected for the three batches in total. The Service is intended for Finnish and international startups, growth companies, research-based teams and potential spin-offs that have progressed beyond the initial idea stage. The primary working language of the Service is English. The Service shall be implemented through a hybrid model, with key in-person activities primarily organised in the Lahti region. The Agreement period is seventeen (17) months, from 1 November 2026 to 31 March 2028. The Tenderer shall state a total price for the Service. The total price may not exceed EUR 180,000 excluding VAT and shall include all costs necessary for the performance of the Service. The price will not be scored. Tenders will be compared solely on the basis of quality, with a weight of 100%. One (1) Supplier will be selected. Tenderers may submit a tender individually or as a consortium. The selected Supplier shall be responsible for the performance of the Service in its entirety, including work performed by consortium members and subcontractors. The detailed scope, requirements, minimum suitability requirements, quality evaluation criteria and contractual terms are specified in the invitation to tender and its annexes.

Hinweis: Zusätzlich zur Gewährträgerhaftung des Landes Schleswig-Holstein für die ZUG.SH AöR wird für das Darlehen eine Kapitaldienstgarantie des Landes bereitgestellt, um Risiken für den Darlehensgeber zu reduzieren und möglichst günstige Zinskonditionen für die ZUG.SH zu erreichen. title: Laboratory-Scale Gas Atomizer
description: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is seeking the supply, delivery, and installation of a laboratory-scale Gas Atomizer (GA) to enhance powder synthesis activities at the Clean Energy Innovation (CEI) facility in Mississauga. At the CEI-Mississauga facility, the development and production of advanced battery materials is one of the core activities. High-quality, spherical metal and alloy powders are crucial in advancing the research on energy materials. Obtaining powders with precise alloy compositions, particle sizes, morphologies, and quality in small quantities from commercial sources poses significant challenges. To address this issue, NRC intends to procure a GA capable of preparing molten alloys with specific compositions and atomizing them using high-speed gas to produce spherical and fine powders.

title: EW038-270709 - Northern Innovation Centre Conceptual Design Study – RFP
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Works & Government Services Canada (PWGSC) requires the services of an architectural firm (Consultant), acting as the Prime Consultant with a multi-disciplinary team of sub-consultants for the delivery of services required for this project. The facility will be located at the Invuik Satellite Station Facility located in Inuvik, Northwest Territories. The Inuvik Satellite Station Facility (ISSF) is an international, multi-use science and technology facility and is located approximately 200km north of the Arctic Circle. NRCan requires the consultant to investigate options of accommodating their program in a modular building vs typical northern construction. A Class C cost estimate and conceptual schematic options developed through this study to seek early project approval to determine the project’s future viability. NRCan requires Pre-design/ Functional Programming and Schematic services to support preliminary costing and design work for a new multi-use modular facility of approximately 1,277m², excluding supporting areas to be proposed by the Prime Consultant and team. For this project, scope is limited to NRCan program requirements only, with future stakeholder participation or expansion to be considered separately once confirmed. Project stakeholder requirements are outlined within the Terms of Reference. See the Terms of Reference for more details.

title: France – Specialist optical instruments – Réalisation et qualification des blocs optiques X de diagnostics plasma pour le Laser Mégajoule
description: Le marché a pour objet l’analyse de la définition technique fournie par le CEA et la démonstration de l’aptitude de cette définition à atteindre les performances spécifiées ainsi que la réalisation, les contrôles et la qualification d’un bloc optique X (BOX) de diagnostics plasma (imageur X-mous) du LMJ. Ce bloc optique est constitué notamment de deux voies de mesure à double miroir, composées chacune d’un miroir plan et d’un miroir torique, inséré sous vide secondaire. Le périmètre de la prestation est le suivant : - l'étude et la réalisation des sous-ensembles opto-mécanique du BOX comprenant la partie mécanique du bloc optique et la partie optique du bloc optique, - l'intégration et pré-alignement du BOX sur un banc optique visible spécifique à définir par le titulaire, - l'assistance à la qualification du BOX sur générateur X sur site CEA, - les équipements et moyens de manutention et outillages de configuration, - les livraisons documentaire associées. Le marché est découpé en : une part ferme comprenant l’analyse du dossier de définition fournis par le CEA ainsi que les justifications optiques et mécaniques détaillées permettant de démontrer la validation de l’ensemble des performances souhaitées ; une part optionnelle comprenant la réalisation, la recette usine et la qualification sur site du BOX et des moyens de soutien, les approvisionnements des matériaux et matériels nécessaires à sa réalisation ; des parts optionnelles supplémentaires concernant des BOX de conception similaire intégrant également des voies d'imagerie à miroirs X.

title: Netherlands – Interpretation services – Tolkdiensten
description: Om de operationele slagkracht van de ILT te versterken, wordt de inkoop van tolkdiensten gecentraliseerd bij één gecontracteerde partij. Medewerkers van de ILT komen tijdens hun taakuitvoering regelmatig in contact met anderstalige partijen, waarbij accurate communicatie cruciaal is voor een rechtmatige handhaving. De huidige overeenkomst voor tolkdiensten verloopt van rechtswege per 31 december 2026. Dit beschrijvend document legt de basis voor een eenduidige marktbenadering, waarmee de ILT één betrouwbare partner selecteert voor alle ad hoc en geplande tolkbehoeften vanaf 1 januari 2027. De scope van deze aanbesteding omvat het leveren van alle benodigde mondelinge, audiovisuele en fysieke tolkdiensten ten behoeve van de ILT. De opdracht omvat zowel de coördinatie, de logistiek als de daadwerkelijke uitvoering van de tolkdiensten in alle benodigde (gangbare en schaarse) talen. Binnen de scope van de af te sluiten overeenkomst wordt onderscheid gemaakt tussen twee vormen van dienstverlening, te weten: 1. ad hoc tolkdiensten; 2. planbare Tolkdiensten. De omvang zal nabij 104.000euro per jaar bedragen.

title: Role Player Support
description: This solicitation is set aside exclusively for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The objective of this requirement is to provide realistic role player support services in support of the Naval Special Warfare Command (NSWC) enterprise. These critical role player services include routine unit-level training exercises as well as periodic, short-notice advanced training exercises, both designed to replicate the complex tactical environments and scenarios encountered by Special Operations Forces (SOF). Role player requirements span eight distinct categories, including specialized linguists, tactical opposing forces (OPFOR), amputee role players, and pyrotechnic/weapons subject matter experts. Offerors are strictly required to read all solicitation documents in full to ensure complete proposal submission compliance. Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement (PWS) contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Due to strict security and dissemination controls, the PWS is password-protected. Prospective offerors shall email the Contracting Point of Contact, Emily Lonigro, at Emily.Lonigro@socom.mil to obtain the access password. All email requests shall explicitly reference solicitation number H9224026QE075 and shall include the requesting firm's Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code as well as their SAM Unique Entity ID (UEI). Offerors shall submit written questions during the quote and proposal preparation period utilizing Attachment S-1 - Q&A. All questions shall be received no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) on 24 September 2026, as only written questions will receive a formal response. To ensure a timely and precise response from the government, each submitted question shall include the document name, document date, specific page, paragraph, clause, or other definitive citation requiring clarification. Final quotes shall be submitted no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) on 14 October 2026. Quotes shall remain valid for no less than 180 days from the date of the RFQ closing.

description: Le projet se décompose de la manière suivante : Un îlot A1 composé de 2 bâtiments A11 et A12. Les bâtiments de l'ilot A1 accueillent 27 logements en accession sociale (PSLA). Les logements proposés vont du T2 au T5 duplex et possèdent tous un balcon ou une terrasse. Certains logements en RDC possèdent aussi des jardins privatifs. Le bâtiment A12 est scindé en deux volumes liés par des passerelles et est en R+2+Combles. Le bâtiment A11 est en R+1+Comble. Le local vélo en RDC est situé en limite de propriété. Un parking, mutualisé entre l'ilot A1 et l'ilot A2, de 118 places se trouve en sous-sol. L'entrée du parking se situe sur l'îlot A1, en limite avec l'îlot A2. Un îlot A2 composé de 3 bâtiments : les bâtiments A21, A22 et A23. Les bâtiments de l'ilot A2 se composent de 30 logements locatifs sociaux. Les logements proposés vont du T2 au T5 duplex et possèdent tous un balcon ou une terrasse. Certains logements en RDC possèdent aussi des jardins privatifs. Le bâtiment A23 est scindé en deux volumes liés par des passerelles et est en R+2+Combles Une crèche et deux locaux associatifs seront livrés brut au RDC du bâtiment A23. Dans le cadre du présent marché, l’attention de l’ENTREPRENEUR est attirée sur le fait que l’opération vise une labellisation RE2020 pour les 2 îlots, ainsi qu’une certification NF Habitat HQE, uniquement pour l’îlot A1.

Federal customers utilize PPM to dispose of excess and surplus property, as well as exchange/sale property, seized and forfeited property, and other categories of personal property. The reuse of personal property assets within the Government saves taxpayer funds, while donation of property to eligible recipients ensures that assets no longer required by the Government continue to benefit the public in communities across the country. When property is sold, sales proceeds may be returned to customer agencies to support their missions or deposited into the U.S. Treasury, as authorized. Additionally, only warranted Sales Contracting Officers may conduct sales of Federal property and award sales contracts to buyers. The Government intends to begin selling unneeded Federal firearms in order to recoup the Government�s investment in these assets when they are no longer required for Federal mission requirements. The Government anticipates selling firearms to Federal Firearms License holders (FFLs), including Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), through negotiated sales or by establishing term sales contracts. Such firearms are classified under Federal Supply Class (FSC) 1005, Guns, through 30mm. FFLs are businesses engaged in the dealing or manufacture of firearms and are licensed by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) pursuant to 18 U.S.C. � 923. The purpose of this RFI is to ascertain the capabilities of FFLs, including OEMs, that may be interested in purchasing unneeded Federal firearms or providing services related to the disposal of such firearms. 3.0 Requested Information: Industry Questions for Industry: How do you determine the fair market value of previously used firearms? What information should the Government provide about each firearm to allow industry to determine fair market value, market interest, and lawful disposition options? How important is physical inspection before purchase? What information would be needed in place of a physical inspection? What types of firearms do you purchase? Are there any types of firearms you will not purchase? If so, why? Do you purchase firearms covered by the National Firearms Act (NFA)? Do you offer shipping and transportation services from firearms sellers, including the Government? If so, how do you coordinate shipping? Do you have the ability to coordinate shipping from a variety of disparate locations and entities across the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories? Do you bear the shipping costs? If so, do you invoice shipping costs separately or reduce fair market value reimbursements to offset shipping costs? Are there minimum quantity requirements for shipping services? What standard practices are used for transportation, pickup, receipt, and chain-of-custody documentation when firearms are transferred from Government or law enforcement sellers? Do you have experience purchasing firearms from Government or law enforcement agencies? What transaction structures are commonly used for sales of Government or law enforcement firearms, such as lot sales, negotiated sales, auctions, term sales contracts, OEM buybacks, or a combination? What legal, regulatory, licensing, transfer, or documentation requirements should the Government consider when selling or disposing of Federal firearms to Federal Firearms Licensees? Do you have experience purchasing firearms derived from seizure or forfeiture? Do you have experience purchasing firearms that are considered historical or collectible? How do you determine the value of historical or collectible firearms? Do you purchase unexpended ammunition? How do you determine the market value of ammunition? description: General Information 2.1 Location Work performed under this scope shall be for and conducted within the VA New Jersey Health Care System (VANJHCS) at the East Orange VA Medical Center, located at 385 Tremont Ave, East Orange, NJ 07018, and Lyons VA Medical Center, located at 151 Knollcroft Rd, Lyons NJ 07939. 2.2 Purpose This Statement of Work (SOW) is for an IDC for demolition and abatement efforts supporting construction and repair services at VANJHCS Medical Centers. All work completed under this contract shall comply with applicable Infection Control requirements and the New Jersey Administrative CodeA (NJAC) 5:23-8, Asbestos Hazard Abatement Subcode, and NJAC 12:120 governing asbestos abatement, licensing, and permitting requirements. Additional administrative and management related requirements are described in Section 3: Requirements. Material testing and air monitoring services required while performing asbestos removal services shall be provided by the VANJHCS at no cost to the contractor. description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) BUILDING 215 ADVANCED MEASUREMENT LABORATORY (AML) CLEANROOM REPAIR AND HEPA FILTER REPLACEMENT Solicitation/Reference No.: 1333ND26RNB190014 1. PURPOSE OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201 to obtain industry feedback concerning the scope, schedule, phasing, cleanroom outage requirements, technical and performance risks, and estimated construction cost associated with the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory (AML) Cleanroom Repair and HEPA Filter Replacement project. NIST previously solicited this requirement under Solicitation No. 1333ND26RNB190014. NIST did not receive an acceptable offer under that solicitation. NIST is therefore reassessing the requirement and acquisition approach before determining whether and how to resolicit the project. NIST is particularly interested in identifying aspects of the requirement that may materially affect industry participation, constructability, schedule feasibility, pricing, risk, or the ability of contractors to submit competitive proposals. Industry is encouraged to provide candid feedback and to identify recommended changes that could improve constructability, competition, schedule feasibility, cost certainty, and overall project execution while continuing to meet NIST�s mission and cleanroom operational requirements. 2. RFI / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE THIS RFI IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND ACQUISITION PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR OTHER SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses to this RFI. Responses will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as offers or proposals that can be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI or for participating in any follow-up discussions. This RFI does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government�s ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be used by NIST in developing or revising the acquisition strategy, statement of work, specifications, schedule, phasing requirements, outage requirements, Government cost estimate, and future solicitation. Respondents should clearly identify and mark any proprietary, confidential, or commercially sensitive information contained in their responses. Respondents should avoid including proprietary information unless necessary to provide a meaningful response. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND The project involves repair and modernization work within the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory cleanroom located at the NIST Gaithersburg Campus. The AML cleanroom encompasses approximately 1,800 square meters and includes approximately 750 square meters of Class 100 cleanroom space. The facility supports sensitive NIST research activities and contains specialized and, in some instances, irreplaceable scientific equipment. The project generally includes, but is not limited to: Replacement of approximately 1,200 terminal supply HEPA filters; Repair and/or modification of HEPA filter connections; Testing, balancing, certification, and recertification of affected HEPA filters and cleanroom spaces; Replacement of approximately 70 variable air volume (VAV) terminal units; Replacement of approximately 54 airflow monitoring devices; Installation of approximately 32 exhaust air control valves; Modification and repair of associated ductwork; Rebalancing of associated air-handling and exhaust systems; Verification and repair, as required, of existing capped ductwork; Controls-related work; Cleaning, testing, balancing, commissioning, and cleanroom certification associated with each affected area; and Protection of existing cleanroom spaces, research operations, and sensitive scientific equipment throughout construction. Detailed project drawings, specifications, and/or relevant portions of the previously issued solicitation may be attached to this RFI or otherwise made available through SAM.gov for purposes of industry review. 4. CURRENT PHASING AND OUTAGE CONCEPT NIST�s previous acquisition strategy was developed to minimize disruption to ongoing research operations by performing the work through phased cleanroom outages rather than shutting down the entire cleanroom for the duration of construction. The previous requirement contemplated 19 construction phases consisting of 18 Critical Cleanroom Outage Phases and one Non-Critical Phase. For each Critical Cleanroom Outage Phase, the contemplated outage period was approximately nine calendar days, generally structured as follows: Outage/construction activities begin at approximately 7:00 p.m. on Friday; Work proceeds continuously, including 24-hour-per-day/seven-day-per-week operations, as necessary; Construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification are completed during the outage period; and The affected cleanroom area is required to achieve Ready for Re-Occupancy by approximately 7:00 a.m. on the second following Monday. Ready for Re-Occupancy generally means that required construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification have been completed; the affected area is operationally capable of supporting its intended use without material restriction; and no deficiencies remain that materially impair safe occupancy or cleanroom operations. The previous requirement also contemplated maintaining unaffected cleanroom bays in operation to the maximum extent practicable and included the possibility of limited additional weekend outages affecting larger portions of the cleanroom. NIST recognizes that these operational constraints may significantly affect contractor staffing, sequencing, subcontractor availability, construction risk, pricing, and schedule feasibility. NIST is specifically seeking industry feedback concerning these requirements. 5. Respondents are not required to answer every question; however, detailed and candid responses are encouraged. A. Risk & Impact Analysis: Explain how the current 24-hour, 9-day limit impacts project risk, labor density, safety, quality assurance, and total cost (including risk contingencies for $8,000/day liquidated damages).
